youtube_title: Kingsbury Ordnance Plant, Indiana: what the war plant left in the ground
youtube:
Lead. Arsenic. Mercury. Explosives. Defense Department cleanup data from 2015 listed them in the ground at the old Kingsbury Ordnance Plant in LaPorte County. In 1940, the Army picked more than 13,000 acres of farmland there for a plant that would load shells for World War 2. It ran again for Korea, then shut down for good. Starting in the 1970s, a solvent company on the old grounds buried thousands of drums of waste, the EPA says (its cleanup dug them up in the 1990s), and it became a Superfund site. In 2022, the EPA called for controls to prevent exposure to its contaminated groundwater. Part of the old plant is now the Kingsbury Fish & Wildlife Area, and its map marks some spots "Contaminated Area/No Trespassing." And the Defense Department's latest data projects its munitions cleanup there won't be finished until 2046. Comment your town, and it could be next! #Kingsbury #LaPorteCounty #Indiana #WW2 #History #LaPorteAfterDark #Shorts

All pictures are drawn. Narration is a computer voice. Sources: ProPublica, "Bombs in Your Backyard" (Defense Department cleanup data, 2015); U.S. Department of Defense, Defense Environmental Restoration Program FY2025 status tables (Table 7); U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Formerly Used Defense Sites program; U.S. EPA, NPL site narrative for Fisher-Calo; U.S. EPA, Superfund Sites in Reuse in Indiana; U.S. EPA, Fisher-Calo five-year reviews (2000, 2025); Indiana DNR, Kingsbury Fish & Wildlife Area maps (2022, 2025); WKVI; Indiana Public Media, A Moment of Indiana History; The History Museum, South Bend. More LaPorte County history: https://laporteweathernow.com/history
